headline: Singular Health (SHG) described as a 'show me story' with US pilot in Puerto Rico as key near-term catalyst
reasoning: Singular Health is an Australian med-tech software company targeting the US healthcare market by addressing workflow bottlenecks around large radiology image files and duplicate imaging — a problem estimated at $17–19 billion. The company has a pilot project in Puerto Rico as a microcosm of the US system, with plans to expand to Florida and Texas and then broader networks if successful. The market is waiting on results before re-rating.
quote: Singular Health is what they call a show me story. The story has been set up really nicely. We've got a pilot project in the US in a little microcosm of the US called Puerto Rico.
episode_title: ASX Market Goss Episode 46 - Howard Digby From Elsight

headline: K-Tech (KTK) pre-IPO heavily oversubscribed within six hours, positioned at intersection of drone and defence thematics
reasoning: K-Tech's prospectus was issued and the books closed in six hours, heavily oversubscribed, driven by the business fundamentals, attractive valuation structuring by CPS, and exposure to both the drone and defence thematics. The CEO had already met pre-IPO revenue targets and tripled capacity with pre-IPO funds, giving Digby high confidence in execution post-listing. Digby joined as non-executive chairman after being impressed by the CEO's track record with pre-IPO capital.
quote: We closed the books in six hours and it was heavily over-subscribed... There's about four things, one is the business which we can go into or not, secondly is the valuation. It's been done very cleverly by Nathan Barbridge at CPS... thirdly, it's also the two thematics, one is drones and the other one is defence.
episode_title: ASX Market Goss Episode 46 - Howard Digby From Elsight

headline: 4DS Memory (4DS) in strategic pause as board navigates direction amid AI bottleneck opportunity for ReRAM technology
reasoning: 4DS is developing ReRAM memory technology aimed at unlocking bottlenecks in AI infrastructure. The company has cash in the bank but is in a cautious period of refocusing investment direction. Digby acknowledged it has been a tough journey with controversial decisions and shareholder criticism, likening it to a biotech with pivots and a long development timeline.
quote: 4DS has got a different approach. And it's in an area that's to do with unlocking the bottlenecks in AI. And that keeps changing all the time. So we're in a little bit of a pause at the moment to just refocus out direction, because we've got cash in the bank, but we want to invest it properly.
episode_title: ASX Market Goss Episode 46 - Howard Digby From Elsight

headline: Drone technology described as the marquee technology of modern warfare, expected to follow aviation's post-WWI growth trajectory
reasoning: Digby draws a parallel between drones today and aircraft after World War I — a technology catapulted by wartime application that subsequently transformed civilian life. He deliberately invests in picks-and-shovels drone exposure (Elsight) rather than individual drone makers, citing inability to pick a winner but high conviction in the overall sector's growth. He expects civilian drone applications to be far larger than military.
quote: Just like airplanes in World War I, right? Before World War I, they had the Wright brothers on their bicycle. After World War I, we almost had passenger airplanes. So that technology catapulted during that time. It'll be the same with drones.
episode_title: ASX Market Goss Episode 46 - Howard Digby From Elsight

headline: Elsight (ELS) highlighted as cash flow positive, capital-light drone communications play exposed to both defence and drone thematics
reasoning: Elsight makes a small communications card placed in assets requiring uninterrupted connectivity, with a focus on drones. The company has caught two hot thematics — defence and drones — and is already cash flow positive and profitable. Management sees the drone industry as analogous to aviation after WWI, with civilian applications being the larger long-term opportunity. Elsight has recently joined the ASX 300, bringing new governance requirements.
quote: It's about that small, and you put it in an asset that you must not lose communication with. It could be anything, an ambulance, a soldier in the field anyway but we've focused on drones. So we've caught the two thematics, defence and drones at the moment and L-Sight's going very well.
episode_title: ASX Market Goss Episode 46 - Howard Digby From Elsight

headline: Leeuwin Wealth actively raises capital for small-cap Western Australian resources companies, seeing ongoing demand for corporate finance services

headline: Leeuwin Wealth advises clients not to panic-sell amid rising rates and global uncertainty, citing diversification as protection
reasoning: Jane Tandy notes that most investors haven't experienced rising interest rates or rising unemployment, but a well-diversified portfolio should weather the volatility. She observes markets have already partially recovered from recent dips and emphasises that panic selling is the wrong response. Advisors can add significant value during periods of uncertainty by keeping clients focused on long-term diversification.
quote: If you've got a well-diversified portfolio, you should always be fine because every different asset class will go up and down over a period of time. And if you have diversified effectively, this is when an advisor provides an enormous amount of value.
episode_title: ASX Market Goss Episode 45 - Jane Tandy From Leeuwin Wealth

headline: Leeuwin Wealth warns investors that holding savings in cash results in negative real returns due to inflation
reasoning: Jane Tandy argues that keeping money in cash means it is going backwards in real terms once inflation is accounted for. She recommends diversifying beyond cash and highlights that superannuation contributions represent a natural starting point for investment exposure. ETF investing is highlighted as a common entry point for younger investors.
quote: If your money is in cash, it's going backwards with inflation. So you really need to be diversifying.
episode_title: ASX Market Goss Episode 45 - Jane Tandy From Leeuwin Wealth

headline: Pitching dual gold and lithium exploration strategy with fresh $7M raise and phase two drilling imminent at Marble Bar

headline: Kali Metals MD sees lithium commodity price cycle turning, justifying retention of lithium assets

episode_title: ASX Market Goss Episode 43 - Paul Adams From Kali Metals

headline: Ardea Resources CEO flags inevitable improvement in nickel equity markets, supporting a bullish long-term outlook for nickel and cobalt producers.

headline: Ardea Resources secures up to $1 billion in indicative funding support from Export Finance Australia and US Ex-Im Bank for its Kalgoorlie Nickel Project, marking a major de-risking milestone.

With Sumitomo Metal Mining and Mitsubishi Corporation as partners and a definitive feasibility study in progress, management believes the project offers multi-decade low-cost production. Penkethman argues the current challenging environment for nickel equities makes now the time to get positioned.
